title: The Candy House the Witch Lives In
notes: Detective-cast (Conan, Ran, Sonoko, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. The old lower-fidelity case file (cases/ep368_...json) correctly identified Fujino as the murderer (s2), so no culprit discrepancy there -- but it flattened his motive to 'unspecified (partially cut off)'; the full transcript gives the real motive explicitly (Hashigaki repeatedly reneged on her promise to let him open his own store after he won a competition with his signature wood chocolate cake roll and worked for her three years). The old file also missed both red-herring motives entirely (Maeda's unpaid debt to the victim, Morimoto's audible pre-murder argument with her) and collapsed the murder weapon into one vague object; the transcript makes clear there are two distinct physical objects -- the wooden log (weapon) and the wood-chocolate cake roll Conan made during Fujino's earlier hands-on demo, which Fujino later 'fixed up' by hiding the log inside its cream and left on his own display stand as apparent evidence of innocence. That early demo scene (Fujino teaching Conan to fork-carve a wood-grain pattern into chocolate cream) is the Chekhov's-gun setup for the disguise trick and was not represented at all in the old file. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Every standard dessert is ruled out as the weapon (cookies shatter, pie and chocolate are too soft, candy too hard to eat alone) -- pointing instead to a log merely disguised as the cake roll, not a dessert weapon at all.
Wood chips, expected only around the cake-carving demo on the showroom floor, also turn up in Fujino's own kitchen -- tying his stand to handling the real log.

edges.detail: loud argument heard from outside minutes before the murder; she refused to join the cake-making demo, confident in her own skill
placed a fake phone call to the office to draw Maeda away from the floor

edges.method: struck in the back of the head with a wooden log disguised as a cake roll
